ICICI Prudential iProtect Smart Plus vs Aditya Birla Sun Life Super Term Plan

Side by side on the figures that decide a claim — and which one we would actually pick.

We score ICICI Prudential iProtect Smart Plus higher at 4.3/5 against 4/5, winning 5 of the 6 comparable measures. iProtect Smart Plus is the cheaper of the two on the illustrated profiles.

Highlighted cells are the better value on that row. Text rows are shown without a winner — deciding that one wording beats another is a judgement, not a measurement.

iProtect Smart Plus

A well-priced plan from a large insurer, and the Smart Exit option is genuinely rare. Where it slips is servicing — 8 complaints per 10,000 claims is roughly eight times HDFC Life. That will not matter for most people, but it is the one number we would want you to see before choosing this over the top two. Good pick if price is the deciding factor and you want a household-name insurer.

Against it

  • 8 complaints per 10,000 claims — the highest of the five by some margin
  • Critical illness rider covers 34 conditions against 60–64 elsewhere
  • Feature depth is thinner than Axis Max or HDFC Life
  • Settlement ratio of 99.30% is good but trails the top two

Super Term Plan

The built-in critical illness cover is the whole argument for this plan, and it is a good one — bundling 42 conditions into the base premium usually beats buying a rider separately. The counterweight is that Aditya Birla Sun Life has the weakest insurer metrics of the five. If you want term and critical illness in a single policy and are comfortable with a 98.70% settlement ratio, this makes sense. If you would rather maximise claim certainty, take Axis Max Life and buy the rider.

Against it

  • At 98.70%, the lowest settlement ratio of the five
  • Solvency of 1.82x is the thinnest here, though still above the 1.5x minimum
  • The critical illness payout is capped at 50% of cover or ₹50 lakh, whichever is lower
  • Smaller distribution footprint in some states

Which one we would pick

ICICI Prudential iProtect Smart Plus, on balance — 4.3/5 against 4/5. Where iProtect Smart Plus is ahead: my insurance bro score, claim settlement ratio, solvency ratio, premium — 30, male, premium — 30, female. Where Super Term Plan is ahead: complaints per 10,000 claims.

A score ranks plans on the evidence available; it cannot know your health history, your dependants or which exclusion will matter to you in ten years. Where the two are close, the deciding factor is usually the text rows above — room rent, waiting periods, exclusions — read against your own circumstances.

Scores are plan features 45%, insurer strength 45%, premium 10% — how we score plans.
